correctness.rationale: Exact cyclotomic factorization has nine distinct irreducible factors; arbitrary divisors are subset products. For each low-level subset, the residue-slice bound T_r≤4 follows from six one-term-per-residue choices of the q-factors and a complete exceptional analysis of ΦqΦ4q and Φ2qΦ4q; reciprocal coefficients control the only delicate product (X+1)ΦqΦ4q. All lifted q² factors are products G(X^q) with |coeff G|≤1, so convolution gives universal height≤4. The explicit disjoint-factor witness has [X³]=4, proving exact height. Independent standard-library integer enumeration verifies 512 divisors for q=3,5,7,11,13; no inference from those finite tests to all q is used.

originality.rationale: The sharp analytic upper bound for all odd primes q at exponent 4q squared, together with the residue-slice invariant, is not stated or implied by the inspected maximal-height papers. Ryan, Bryan C. Ward and Ryan Ward formulated the square-prime-pair extremizer as a conjecture, computed finite cases only, and already established the lower bound. Kaplan and Decker--Moree treat p-squared times q, not both squared; Wang addresses p times q-to-b, not four times q squared. Indexed research records found no statement with equivalent objects and quantified scope. A literature omission remains possible.

value.rationale: The height B(n) is a natural, previously studied invariant; the 2010 authors explicitly posed the two-prime-squared extremizer problem and computed only finite parameters. An exact infinite subclass, settling p=2 of their conjecture, is a substantive nonroutine answer. The new structural residue-class coefficient-mass inequality explains a dimension-independent bound and supplies a reusable technique, not a numerical restatement or an arbitrary slice.
